newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 28.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Randle rape claim 'not retracted': An allegation of rape against Hurricanes rugby player Roger Randle had not been retracted, though the matter would not be pursued in court, a South African attorney-general said on Tuesday. Page 1.
Joint caucus seeks to ease tension: National and NZ First will seek to improve strained Coalition relations at a joint caucus meeting scheduled for June 17. Page 2.
Call for ACT to name 'parlour' MP: Acting Labour leader Michael Cullen has called for ACT NZ to name the MP it says ran up thousands of dollars of debt at a Wellington massage parlour. Page 2.

Caygill backs removing student funding cap: Removing the cap on the number of student places the government was prepared to fund was the most straightforward step it could take to reform tertiary funding, former finance minister David Caygill said on Tuesday. Page 2.
Clear moves into business market: Clear Communications will today announce its move into the lucrative business local call market. Page 17.

Salomon downgrades Telecom shares: Salomon Brothers Asia-Pacific said it was downgrading its recommendation on Telecom shares to hold from buy "because the upturn in the company's business appears to be moving further into the future". Page 17.
Dairy Board wins cheese ruling: The Dairy Board has had its tribulations in Britain with butter export disputes but in Peru it has won a court victory on cheese names. Page 17.

Inflation pressure low in productive sector: Statistics NZ issued measures of the prices paid and charged by producers of goods and services on Tuesday, confirming that inflation pressure is low in the productive sector. Page 17.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Shipley's long road to better funding base: The country is being steered towards a radical shake-up of the roading system which could bring road tolls, higher road user charges and petrol taxes, and lead to highways being turned into a state-owned enterprise.
Stephan rejects $0.5m: Out-of-work juice entrepreneur Stephan Lepionka has reportedly turned down $500,000 for his quarter share in the Wellington-based Fresh Juice Company.
Health fees will hurt cost of living: A new round of increases in medical insurance premiums is likely to affect inflation just as it did last year, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday.

CDL meetings off to a positive start: The CDL hotel and property group's first annual meeting of the week was a positive but quiet affair, signalling tough times for the industry, but optimism for trade two years out.
Telecom buying boosts price: Telecom has spent $444 million so for in its $1 billion share buyback.
Power NZ shareholders revolt: Power New Zealand's small shareholders are standing in the way of the proposed full takeover of their company by Mercury Energy and Unicorp of the United States.
Ceramco's cups expected to sag: Ceramco Corporation will, at best, report a break-even result for its March 31 financial year today largely because of continuing problems in its apparel division.
THE PRESS

Chch club siphons gaming funds: The Papanui Working Men's Club siphoned more than $1 million from its gaming machine profits over several years to prop up its ailing finances, an accountant's confidential report shows. Page 1.

Regulations threat made over tobacco: Regulation would be the only answer if the tobacco industry continued to ignore people's health needs and kept producing cigarettes with "irresponsibly" high nicotine levels, Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton said on Tuesday night. Page 3.
Squash costly for Grocorp: Grocorp Pacific's restructuring programme did not come in time to stop losses on its squash growing operation. Page 28.

Bonus scrip to Fletcher investors: Shareholders in Fletcher Challenge's Building, Energy, and Paper divisions will next month receive four fully-paid Forests shares for every 100 shares held. Page 28.

Kingsgate confident of lift: Kingsgate International Corporation is confident that this year's after-tax profit will be better than the $2.56 million earned last year, with its two main Sydney assets producing improved income. Page 29.
